vo: This vole never heard a thing.

label: 5 seconds earlier
vo: Five seconds earlier. The owl lands, prey already in its talons.

label: 1 minute earlier
vo: One minute earlier, the vole was hiding under the snow. Invisible. Safe. Or so it thought.
But the owl's face works like a satellite dish. It funnels the faintest scratching straight into its ears.
It doesn't need to see. It locks on by sound alone.
And here's the terrifying part. Its wing feathers have tiny combs on the edge that break the air apart.
The whoosh that would give any other bird away... almost vanishes.
Talons first. Over in a second.

label: The real reason
vo: And it was no accident. Short-eared owls follow the voles. When vole numbers boom, the owls arrive.
That vole was hunted... long before it ever saw the owl.
